subject: Acme - Rate limits, burst / overage pricing follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Follow-up: rate limits / burst usage & pricing (recap + next steps)

Hi Jordan / Samantha - thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can prepare a tailored pricing/ops proposal:

Summary of what I heard from the call:
- Baseline traffic: roughly 200M tokens / month for Product X (mostly generation + few embeddings).
- Peak patterns: spikes up to ~500M tokens in a few product launch windows (bursts lasting 5-15 minutes, concurrency up to ~600 rps).
- Avg tokens per call: ~350 tokens (requests + responses).
- Target latency: p95 < 600ms for interactive flows.
- Primary ask: want clarity on how Redwood handles short-term bursts, quota increases, and what overage rates look like.
- Budget guidance you mentioned: target $/1M tokens in the $30 range if possible.

Clarifying questions for the proposal:
1) Do you expect the 200M baseline to be steady month-over-month or is that expected to grow (and by how much)?
2) For bursts: are those unpredictable (e.g., marketing-driven) or scheduled (campaign windows we can anticipate)?
3) Any regulatory/data residency constraints for this workload?

Next steps we propose:
- I'll send a short note with our suggested rate-limit/overage model and a couple of pricing scenarios (baseline committed vs. pay-as-you-go + overage multipliers).
- Camila (cc) can run through a technical plan for a proof-of-concept to validate burst behavior and latency at scale.
- If this looks good, we'll follow with a draft quote + procurement steps (PO/DocuSign).

I attached a short primer that outlines our rate-limit patterns and typical overage terms (Redwood-RateLimits-Overage-Tiers.pdf).

Can you confirm the answers to the three clarifying questions above and any other constraints we should account for?

Thanks - talk soon.

--
Marissa

Thanks Marissa - appreciate the recap. A few answers below:

1) Baseline growth: we expect ~10-15% month-over-month growth for the next 6 months as we onboard a couple of large enterprise customers, so baseline is likely to drift upward.
2) Bursts: mostly unpredictable (marketing + unexpected user events). We can share historical spike windows but they aren't always scheduled. Bursts typically last 5-15 minutes and happen a few times per month.
3) Residency: US only for now. No special restrictions beyond standard SOC2 expectations.

A couple more details to help with pricing:
- Baseline: ~200M tokens/mo
- Launch peaks: short windows pushing total to ~500M tokens/mo in peak months (so monthly usage can spike)
- Concurrency: baseline ~50 rps, bursts up to ~600 rps for short windows
- Budget target: ideally around $30 / 1M tokens (we know that depends on commit)

Please send a couple of pricing scenarios (payg, committed 200M, committed 1B) and how overages are charged (per-token multiplier? monthly cap?). We’ll loop procurement once we have a draft quote.

--
Jordan Miles
Head of Product | Acme Corp
jordan.miles@acmecorp.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Miles <jordan.miles@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, procurement@acmecorp.com
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: rate limits / burst usage & pricing (recap + next steps)

Great - thanks for the detail, Jordan. I'll outline three high-level options below (these are for discussion; we can refine with legal/procurement):

Option A - Pay-as-you-go (no commit)
- Unit price: $75 / 1M tokens (list)
- Overage: billed at list price; short-term quota increases handled case-by-case (support SLA for emergency cap increases)

Option B - Mid-level commit (200M/mo commit)
- Committed unit price: $45 / 1M tokens
- Baseline reserved capacity to improve latency during bursts
- Overage: billed at 1.25x committed price (so $56.25 / 1M) for usage above commit in the billing period

Option C - Enterprise commit (1B/mo commit)
- Committed unit price: $30 / 1M tokens
- Includes priority for short-term burst capacity and a dedicated runway for quota increase requests
- Overage: billed at 1.1x committed price (so $33 / 1M) within negotiated thresholds; above that we'd evaluate capacity and may suggest temporary reserved capacity

How we handle bursts & quota increases (high-level):
- Soft rate limits for interactive routes with short burst window (we allow short spikes up to ~3x baseline RPS for 5-15 minutes, subject to churn impact on other customers)
- For predictable or sustained high concurrency we recommend Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) or a committed contract so we can allocate pool capacity
- Emergency quota increases: account team + support can approve a limited temporary increase (typically within 24-48 hours for customers with committed capacity; may take longer for payg)

I attached the short primer (Redwood-RateLimits-Overage-Tiers.pdf) that describes typical windows and examples. Camila - can you confirm the burst policy language & suggested test plan?

If that looks reasonable I'll put together a draft quote (we can show the three scenarios) and a sample PO / DocuSign to move procurement along.

--
Marissa

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Miles <jordan.miles@acmecorp.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Follow-up: rate limits / burst usage & pricing (recap + next steps)

Adding a quick SE note - thanks for the traffic details, Jordan. A few actionable items from the technical side:

- Recommended approach for predictable behaviour: 1) start with a staged POC on Hosted API with traffic shaping to reproduce burst windows, 2) if bursts are frequent/sustained move to Dedicated capacity with autoscaling pools.
- Soft quotas vs. hard quotas: we use soft rate limits to avoid hard failures; soft limits return 429 with headers that indicate retry-after and recommended backoff. For interactive UX we recommend a short client-side retry/backoff plus local cache where appropriate.
- Burst configuration example: allow baseline RPS + allow short-term burst up to 3x for 10 minutes with per-minute decay; this keeps latency stable for other customers.
- Overage mechanics: billing is per-token on invoice. For customers with committed capacity we typically apply a multiplier to the committed unit price for overage (Marissa's examples above). For payg customers, overage is billed at list price.
- Test plan: we suggest a 2-week POC with a ramp: 10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% of expected baseline over rolling days, insert synthetic bursts (5-15 minutes) to validate latency and retry behavior. We can run the POC on a mirror of your traffic pattern if you share the anonymized CSV (I referenced Acme-MAAP-usage-estimates.xlsx).

I'll prepare a short runbook for the POC and share it after the SE call.

--
Camila Reyes
